caption:
How a story gets from a journal to this feed. Every candidate is scored for reach and for solidity; it ships only if the scores add to 14 or more and solidity is at least 6. Every number on screen needs two independent sources. GREEN ships, AMBER ships with the caveat on screen, RED does not. This week the fact-check pulled two of twelve stories. Corrections pinned within 24 hours. What should we check harder?

#science #factcheck #behindthescenes #scicomm

slides.title: How we check a story *before* you see it
slides.sub: Our pipeline, from intake to a pinned correction.

slides.title: Intake
items: Two research desks file candidate stories every **Monday**
Each one carries the finding, the **venue and date**, a URL, and its caveats

slides.title: Two scores: *V* and *S*
slides.body: V is virality potential, S is scientific solidity, each from 1 to 10. A story ships only if V + S is at least 14 and S is at least 6. An S of 5 or less runs only as an explicit 'contested' piece, never as a finding.

slides.myth: One link in the caption means it is verified
slides.fact: Every number on screen needs two independent sources
slides.body: One source is a claim. Two that do not copy each other is a check.

slides.title: The gate
items: _AMBER_ ships with the caveat written on screen, not only in the caption

slides.title: stories pulled by the fact-check
slides.body: One paper turned out to be from June, not September. One headline claim appeared nowhere in the journal's own account. Both are on hold until the papers are opened.

slides.title: Source on the last slide, *every time*
slides.body: And if we get something wrong, the correction goes into a pinned comment on the post within 24 hours.
